target.title: fix(browser): don't finalize/archive on implausibly short mid-stream captures (#284)
target.body:
Addresses the outcome-based completion-guard half of #284 (the part #285 and #289 don't cover).

## The failure

Per the reporter's second data point on #284: the thinking status flapped (`no thinking status` → `active/inline` → `no thinking status`) while generation continued, and at ~6m the CLI concluded the answer was complete, captured a **single character** (`Answer: I`, `↓1`), then **archived the conversation** — after which no tab-level recovery was possible.

## Root cause

`waitForAssistantResponse` runs a DOM-observer evaluation racing a snapshot watchdog. When the evaluation path wins mid-stream during a thinking-UI transition, there's a window where the **stop button is already gone** (thinking UI torn down) but **completion controls haven't appeared yet** (answer not rendered). The fast path only reconfirms a capture against the stability watchdog when `stopVisible || completionVisible`:

```ts
if (stopVisible || completionVisible) {
  const completed = await pollAssistantCompletion(...);
  ...
}
return candidate; // <-- otherwise the stub is trusted as final
```

In the flapping window both are false, so a stub capture (`"I"`) is returned unconfirmed. A downstream run can then archive on it.

## Fix

Add a third confirmation trigger: an **implausibly short capture** (< 16 chars). The decision is a pure function:

```ts
export function shouldConfirmAssistantCompletion({ candidateLength, stopVisible, completionVisible }) {
  if (stopVisible || completionVisible) return true;
  return candidateLength > 0 && candidateLength < MIN_CONFIDENT_ANSWER_LENGTH; // 16
}
```

Why length alone (not "short relative to elapsed time" as the issue speculated): the watchdog is a **safe confirmation, not a rejection** — it only ever returns a capture that is `>=` the candidate length, and a genuinely short reply passes it unchanged (stable text, stop button gone). So confirming *all* short captures costs a few seconds of stability-window latency on tiny answers but never drops valid content, and there's no time threshold to tune. A mid-stream stub, by contrast, either keeps growing or the stop button reappears — and the watchdog then captures the real answer. The 16-char boundary matches the existing `shortAnswer` handling already inside `pollAssistantCompletion`.

Archive is left untouched on purpose: once completion is no longer premature, the stub never reaches the archive path, so this stays a focused capture-layer fix rather than conflating with the archive/reattach surfaces #289 touches.

## Verification

- `pnpm run check` clean; `pnpm vitest run` — 1395 passed, 43 skipped, 0 failed.
- 6 new unit tests on `shouldConfirmAssistantCompletion` covering both control-visible triggers, the short-capture trigger, the confident-length pass-through, the empty-capture case, and the 15/16 boundary.
- Adjusted two pre-existing `pageActions` tests whose fixtures used a 6-char `"Answer"` payload incidental to what they assert (background-poller abort / payload return) — bumped to a confident-length answer so they exercise the direct fast-path return they intend, rather than the new short-capture confirmation.

Live note: I could not stage the mid-stream flapping race on demand (it's a UI-transition timing race), and a clean live no-regression smoke was blocked today by ChatGPT session-token rotation in my test profile. The change is safe by construction (confirmation never rejects content) and unit-covered at the decision boundary; happy to add a live capture if a maintainer can reproduce the flap.
